answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region during peak settlement, so the highest-leverage single move is to shift writes off that region. Rollback is disallowed by the security-patch constraint (b1 is historically effective but not usable). Circuit breaking (b4) would fail writes, which violates the no-lost-writes objective. Read-replica routing (b5) addresses report/read load, not the write path. Adding capacity (b3) helped when headroom was provisioned before a peak, not as a mid-surge regional write-path fix. b2 is the closest prior: regional failover restored latency with a clean traffic shift; verifying that record before commit. Flagging downstream settlement-value risk because writes are heavy at daily peak; archive details of b2 may still change blast-radius or write-safety assumptions.
